title: Track, reconcile and report: the monthly workflow

say: Track, reconcile and report: the monthly workflow.
This is the video for Module 2 of Marketing Analytics and Reporting.
Every report is only as good as the tracking under it. So first you set up GA4, Google's free analytics tool, and tag every link you share.

panel.heading: Three jobs you repeat every month
items: Track: GA4 key events and tagged links
Reconcile: all sources in one sheet
Report: one page, checked insights

say: Then you bring ad platforms, analytics and payments into one sheet, and explain why they disagree.

say: Finally, you turn it into a one-page report that a busy owner reads in five minutes. This is the workflow you will repeat for every client or employer.

say: GA4 records actions as events. Mark the ones that matter as key events. Many Nigerian businesses close sales on WhatsApp, so track chat button clicks too, but report them apart from orders. A click shows interest, not payment.

cards.d: Mark purchase, or a WhatsApp chat click, as a key event. Test each one yourself.
Set it to 14 months, and match time zone and currency to the business.
Never send names, phone numbers or emails into GA4. Ask consent where required.

say: Set data retention to 14 months, and use the business's time zone and currency, for example Africa slash Lagos and naira.

say: Without tags, many visits from chat apps land in Direct, with no channel. UTM parameters are labels added to the end of a link. For example, Funke sells cakes in Ibadan. She gives her campaign one lowercase name.

panel.heading: Funke tags her Christmas cake campaign
items: Always set utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign
One campaign name: xmas_cakes_2026
WhatsApp: source whatsapp, medium social
Ads: medium paid_social; newsletter: email
Record every link, test it in GA4 Realtime

say: Her WhatsApp broadcast link uses source whatsapp and medium social. Instagram ads use medium paid social, and the newsletter uses email, so GA4 sorts each into the right channel.

say: No single tool sees everything. Each ad platform credits sales by its own rules, and Meta can even count people who only saw the ad. Both may claim the same order.

panel.heading: Why the numbers disagree
items: Each platform uses its own rules and windows
Meta and Google can claim the same order
Ad blockers and refused cookies hide sales
WhatsApp and phone orders never reach GA4
Different time zones or date ranges

say: Tracking gaps hide some sales, WhatsApp orders never reach GA4 unless you add them, and mismatched settings shift results between days.

items: Each platform uses its own rules and windows

say: Her Paystack dashboard and WhatsApp order list show 86 paid orders worth 2,064,000 naira.
She spent 400,000 naira on Meta and 250,000 on Google Ads. Meta claims 58 purchases. Google claims 41. Together that is 99, which is 13 more than the orders actually paid.
So she leads with figures from real money. Total spend 650,000 naira. MER about 3.18. Blended cost per order about 7,558 naira. Channel costs are shown as a range, because platforms and GA4 disagree.
Use platform numbers to tune inside each platform. Never add or average two platforms' ROAS. That counts double-claimed sales twice.
Use payments to judge the whole budget. Match spend to billing, revenue to settlements, and remove refunds before you trust the sheet.
Looker Studio is Google's free report tool. Put revenue, orders, spend, MER and cost per order at the top, then a weekly trend line.

panel.heading: A one-page report that works
items: Top: scorecards vs the previous period
Middle: weekly revenue and spend trend
Channel table with cost per purchase range
Three insights: what, so what, now what
Footer: sources, dates, rule, known gaps

say: Add a channel table, three insights you write yourself, each ending in an action, and honest caveats at the bottom.

say: Create MER as a calculated field from summed revenue and summed spend. Averaging weekly ratios gives a wrong answer.
And watch your words. Conversion moving from 1.1% to 1.4% is up 0.3 percentage points, or 27% relative.

panel.rule: Build ratios from totals. Never average a column of ratios.

say: Before sending, run five checks. Spend matches billing. Revenue matches payments. The same date range everywhere. Ratios built from totals. Caveats written down.
These catch most errors that destroy trust.

panel.heading: Five quality checks
items: Spend matches billing
Revenue matches payments
Same date range everywhere
Ratios built from totals
Caveats written down

say: To remember. Tag every link in lowercase. Keep personal data out of GA4. Treat payments as the source of truth, and lead with blended figures. Every insight should end in an action someone owns.
